title: Asymmetric magnetoresistance in 3$d$-5$d$ based La$_{0.67}$Ca$_{0.33}$MnO$_3$/SrIrO$_3$ bilayer: The role of unidirectional anisotropy
authors: A. G. A. Rahman, Subham Naskar, R. K. Patel, S. Manna, Chandrani Nath, Kranti Kumar, A. K. Pramanik
abstract: The complex interplay between spin-orbit coupling, magnetism, and magnetic field at the interface of a heterostructure consisting of ferromagnet (FM) and heavy metal (HM), often exhibit extraordinary magnetic and electric phenomena where an in-plane Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction plays a crucial role to stabilize local spin texture in FM layer. Here, we report detailed magnetic and magneto-transport behaviour on an epitaxially grown thin heterostructure with 3$d$ FM La$_{0.67}$Ca$_{0.33}$MnO$_3$ (LCMO) and 5$d$ HM SrIrO$_3$ (SIO). Magnetic measurements show an unusual development of magnetic ordering in SrIrO3 around 42 K, which further leads to a Mn/Ir magnetic coupling at the interface. The magnetoresistance (MR) measurements show an evolution of its value and shape with the magnetic state of this bilayer. While MR is negative at high temperature, it shows a positive to negative crossover with stable magnetic ordering of LCMO, and finally the positive MR exhibits an asymmetry at low temperature with the ordering of SIO. While we ascribe this unusual MR behaviour to interface-driven varying spin scattering between itinerant and localized electrons, our results shed a light to comprehend the complex but tunable interface behavior on charge transport in a particularly designed heterostructure, offering valuable insights for future functional material engineering.
summary: This work reports on the magnetic and magneto-transport properties of a $	ext{LCMO}/	ext{SIO}$ heterostructure. The researchers found that the magnetoresistance exhibits complex, asymmetric behavior linked directly to the magnetic ordering of both the $3d$ and $5d$ layers. This suggests that interfacial spin scattering is a crucial, tunable mechanism for controlling charge transport in these correlated magnetic materials.
main_problem: Investigating the origin and tuning of asymmetric magnetoresistance (MR) in a $3d$-$5d$ magnetic heterostructure.
main_result: The unusual MR behavior is attributed to interface-driven varying spin scattering between itinerant and localized electrons, demonstrating tunable interfacial magnetic transport.
method: The study combines epitaxial thin-film growth (PLD) with comprehensive characterization, including magnetic measurements (SQUID) and electrical transport measurements (four-probe technique).
model_or_system: The system is an epitaxially grown bilayer of a $3d$ ferromagnet, $	ext{La}_{0.67}	ext{Ca}_{0.33}	ext{MnO}_3$ (LCMO), and a $5d$ heavy metal, $	ext{SrIrO}_3$ (SIO), on an $	ext{STO}$ substrate. The physics involves the interplay of spin-orbit coupling, magnetism, and interfacial interactions.
key_observables: Magnetoresistance (MR), resistivity $ho(T)$, magnetization $M(H)$, and magnetic ordering temperatures ($	ext{T}_c$ for LCMO, $	ext{T}_p$ for SIO).
important_parameters: Temperature (especially near magnetic ordering points), applied magnetic field ($H$), and interfacial coupling strength.
main_assumptions: The unusual MR behavior is ascribed to interface-driven varying spin scattering between itinerant and localized electrons.
figures_summary: Figures confirm epitaxial growth (XRD), show smooth film morphology (AFM), detail magnetic transitions in both layers (ZFC/FC, M(H)), and present the temperature and field dependence of the MR.
paper_structure: The paper follows a standard experimental structure: structural characterization (XRD, AFM, SEM) $	o$ magnetic characterization (SQUID) $	o$ transport measurements ($ho(T)$, MR) $	o$ interpretation linking MR evolution to the magnetic state of the bilayer.
why_interesting: The study explores how interfacial magnetic coupling (via DM interaction and SOC) dictates charge transport properties, which is a key area for understanding correlated electron behavior in engineered quantum materials.
